data.one_liner: Pure‑Dart client for the Pusher Channels real‑time protocol.
data.what_it_does: Provides a WebSocket‑based client that connects to Pusher Channels, handling authentication, subscription to public, private, presence and encrypted channels, and event binding/triggering. It abstracts the protocol details and offers reconnection and activity‑ping handling.
use_when: You need real‑time messaging via Pusher Channels across mobile, web and desktop.
You want a cross‑platform Dart/Flutter solution without native plugins.
You require support for presence and encrypted private channels.
avoid_when: You are using a different real‑time backend (e.g., Firebase, Supabase).
You need fallback transports like long‑polling or SSE.
strengths: Cross‑platform (Android, iOS, web, Windows, macOS, Linux).
Supports all Pusher channel types (public, private, presence, encrypted).
Stream‑based API integrates well with RxDart and Flutter streams.
weaknesses: Limited to Pusher Channels only; not a generic WebSocket client.
No built‑in UI widgets; you must handle UI updates yourself.
Relies on web_socket_channel; advanced reconnection strategies may require custom code.

alternatives.name: web_socket_channel
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides a lower‑level WebSocket API; you can implement the Pusher protocol yourself if you need full control or a lighter dependency.
